judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 1 Indicators (same statement-type grain, same coordinate rank 0) that engage early spelling: B1.5.10.1.1 (Strand 5 Using Writing Conventions / Sub-Strand 10 Spelling, under 'Use phonics knowledge to spell words') asks learners to identify and spell simple words correctly, while B1.4.4.1.1 (Strand 4 Writing / Sub-Strand 4 Labelling Items, under 'Draw and label simple objects') asks learners to draw simple pictures and use invented spelling to write about oneself. Their LCs ('Spell simple words correctly', 'Identify simple words' vs 'Use invented spelling to write about oneself', 'Draw simple pictures...') show genuine, complementary coherence — accurate word-level spelling and emergent/invented spelling applied in a drawing-and-labelling writing task. This is substantive skill coherence rather than a justified dependency: at the same grade rank the evidence does not establish that proficiency in one materially supports success in the other (invented spelling is deliberately non-conventional, and the accurate-spelling indicator sits in a different strand/sub-strand purpose), so a directional buildsTowards is not supported. Nomination signals (shared Grade ancestor, weak 'b1' code prefix, single shared tokens 'simple'/'spelling') are proximity evidence only and were not treated as verdicts. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated, limiting fuller exemplar context.

judgment.rationale: B3.5.4.1.3 (Strand 5: Using Writing Conventions/Grammar Usage, Sub-Strand: Using Action Words) asks learners to use simple past and past continuous verb forms to express past actions, while B3.4.14.1.1 (Strand 4: Writing, Sub-Strand: Informative/Academic Writing, under content standard 'Write on the events of the day') asks learners to write picture events using simple sentences. There is substantive coherence: past-tense verb control is a grammar resource naturally exercised when composing simple sentences recounting events, so the two reinforce each other as complementary grammar and composition skills. However, both sit at the same BASIC 3 coordinate (rank 2) in different strands, and the only lexical overlap is the generic token 'simple' (jaccard ~0.06); the writing indicator does not specify past-tense forms and the grammar indicator does not specify extended writing, so no same-rank developmental dependency in either direction is substantively evidenced. Endpoint source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, which limits deeper inference but does not undermine the symmetric coherence reading.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 1 Indicators (same statement-type grain, identical coordinate rank 0) addressing narrative comprehension: B1.2.7.2.3 (Reading / Sub-Strand 7: Comprehension, under CS B1.2.7.2 'Use knowledge skills and techniques of reading to understand') asks learners to connect ideas and information in stories to own experience and world knowledge, while B1.1.7.1.2 (Oral Language / Sub-Strand 7: Listening Comprehension, under CS B1.1.7.1 'Use appropriate skills and strategies to process meaning from texts') asks learners to recognise and relate the sequence of events in a narrative text. Their LCs ('connect ideas and information in stories...' vs 'recognise/relate the sequence of events in stories') show genuine conceptual coherence around making meaning from narrative, but they sit in different strands and modalities (reading vs listening) and target distinct comprehension strategies (personal connection vs event sequencing). With equal grade rank and no source evidence that one strategy is assumed by the other, a directional buildsTowards is not substantiated; the shared token overlap is largely function words and the shared 'stories'/'b1' signals are weak. Symmetric, mutually reinforcing narrative-comprehension coherence supports relatesTo. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence (and one endpoint's LC metadata) is truncated and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context.

judgment.rationale: Both are Indicator-grain statements in Strand 1: Oral Language, Sub-Strand 9 (Giving and Responding to Commands, Instructions, Directions and Making Requests) under the parallel Content Standards B2.1.9.1 and B3.1.9.1. The BASIC 2 indicator (rank 1) is receptive only: 'Respond to commands, instructions and requests' (LCs: respond to commands/instructions/requests). The BASIC 3 indicator (rank 2) is 'Make and respond to polite requests' (LCs: make polite requests, respond to polite requests), which extends the same request-handling skill by adding productive formulation and a politeness/register demand. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 3 (rank 2) Indicators sharing the same parent Content Standard B3.1.6.1 'Explore using certain culturally acceptable language for communication' within Strand 1 Oral Language, Sub-Strand 6 Conversation. B3.1.6.1.4 asks learners to use a wider variety of words to talk about different customs and cultural values (vocabulary breadth applied to cultural topics); B3.1.6.1.2 asks learners to talk about events in the community (oral expression about local happenings). These are substantively coherent sibling oral-conversation skills about community and cultural life that reinforce one another, but the evidence shows no clear developmental dependency: at equal grade rank the only ordering signals are sibling code sequence and adjacent source pages, which alone are not semantic, and neither statement's text indicates that one capability is presupposed by the other. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment; shared ancestry and the weak 'talk/about' token overlap were not treated as progression evidence. Endpoint source evidence is truncated and both endpoints and all ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context (the Content Standard and the BASIC 3 grade organizer are merged records), which limits but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Indicators (rank 1, same grade coordinate) within STRAND 4: WRITING, but in different sub-strands: B2.4.3.1.2 'Use lower and upper case letters appropriately in words and simple sentences' (Sub-Strand 3: Writing Letters – Small and Capital, under B2.4.3.1 on letter-sound/letter knowledge for legible writing) and B2.4.4.1.1 'Draw and label objects found in their environment' (Sub-Strand 4: Labelling Items, under B2.4.4.1 'Draw and label simple pictures'). They are coherent complementary writing tasks: letter-case conventions are the mechanics of forming written words, while labelling applies writing to drawn objects (LCs: 'draw objects...', 'label objects found in their environment'). However, the labelling indicator and its LCs make no reference to case conventions, words, or sentences, and the shared nomination signals are weak (only 'and'/'in' token overlap, weak code-prefix b2/4, adjacent pages 78/79). With equal rank, there is no substantive pair-specific evidence that proficiency in either is developmentally required for or clearly supportive of the other, so symmetric conceptual coherence within the Writing strand is the supported judgment rather than a directional buildsTowards.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 2 Indicators (rank 1, same coordinate) in Strand 2: Reading, but sit under different Sub-Strands and Content Standards: B2.2.9.1.1 'Read texts/stories/passages with good pace, accuracy and expression' under Sub-Strand 9: Fluency / B2.2.9.1 'Read texts fluently', and B2.2.7.2.5 'Use visualisation strategy (form mental images about texts) to enhance understanding of level-appropriate texts' under Sub-Strand 7: Comprehension / B2.2.7.2 'Use knowledge skills and techniques of reading to understand and interpret texts'. They are complementary same-grade reading capabilities (oral fluency performance vs. a mental comprehension strategy) that reinforce reading of texts, and the shared LC tag 'reading' and token 'texts' support substantive coherence. At equal rank the evidence gives no source-backed warrant that proficiency in one specifically supports success in the other within this curriculum's stated sequencing, so a symmetric relatesTo is preferred over either buildsTowards direction. Source-evidence truncation on both endpoints and truncated LC metadata on the second endpoint limit finer-grained interpretation but do not affect the statement texts relied upon here.
